name: Cosmopolitan democracy
summary: Cosmopolitan democracy holds that democratic norms and procedures should be extended beyond the nation-state, because global decisions affect people who have no vote over them. It proposes reforming the UN, expanding international criminal and judicial bodies and creating a world parliamentary assembly, as global governance with layered authority rather than a single world state. Its advocates reject exporting democracy by force and favour nonviolence, popular control and political equality.
scope: The programme of David Held and Daniele Archibugi (Democracy and the Global Order, 1995; Cosmopolitan Democracy: An Agenda for a New World Order, 1995; Archibugi's The Global Commonwealth of Citizens, 2008), with Held's social-democratic version of it as a secondary strand. Excludes world federalism of the Einstein kind and general moral cosmopolitanism. Most statements on domestic economics, religion and social issues are not addressed by its texts and are answered with low confidence by inference from its liberal-democratic and social-democratic commitments.

keyFigures.name: David Held
keyFigures.role: British political theorist who developed the model of cosmopolitan democracy and global social democracy.

keyFigures.name: Daniele Archibugi
keyFigures.role: Italian political theorist who co-founded the project and wrote its fullest book-length case, The Global Commonwealth of Citizens.

sources.title: Cosmopolitan democracy
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview: global governance without world government, ICC, world parliament, scepticism of military intervention, key works and critics.

sources.usedFor: Archibugi's proposals: UN reform, advisory world parliament, supplementing and constraining states, humanitarian intervention, self-determination, no export of democracy by force.

sources.title: Demos and Cosmopolis

sources.usedFor: Opening argument that popular sovereignty can only be recovered in a cosmopolitan order above the nation-state (only the free portion was opened).

sources.title: Review of The Global Commonwealth of Citizens
sources.author: Luis Cabrera, Ethics & International Affairs 24.1 (2010)
sources.usedFor: Nonviolence, popular control and equal participation principles; UN centrality; humanitarian intervention capacity; thin global citizenship.

sources.title: David Held (1951-2019), tribute by Daniele Archibugi
sources.author: Democracy Without Borders
sources.usedFor: Held's global social democracy and fear of rule by wealthy technocrats.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Held's call for global social democracy to sustain justice and well-being implies support for state-guaranteed basic services, though the sources never discuss healthcare itself.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from Held's social-democratic emphasis on justice and well-being; wage policy is not discussed in the sources.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Held's global social democracy wants markets embedded in democratic law, so adherents would reject the strong claim that markets beat governments.

public-ownership.rationale: Social-democratic leanings point toward public provision, but the sources do not take a position on nationalisation and adherents likely differ.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from Held's global social democracy and his fear that a few wealthy technocrats could rule everyone; no tax figures are cited.

unions-good.rationale: Social-democratic stance and the emphasis on affected people having a voice suggest support, but unions are not discussed.

property-fundamental.rationale: A global social democrat would treat property as subject to democratic law and justice, not as nearly inviolable.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Cosmopolitan democracy aims to subject powerful economic actors to democratic accountability, so tighter regulation of corporations fits its aims.

cut-welfare.rationale: Held's global social democracy supports welfare provision; the dependency argument is not one the sources attribute to adherents.

worker-ownership.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses ownership of firms; adherents range from liberal-market to social-democratic views.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Strong commitment to human rights and accountable power suggests wariness of surveillance, but the topic is not discussed in the sources.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy falls outside the project and liberal adherents are split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The sources do not address speech law; liberal-democratic adherents are divided between legal restriction and free speech.

strong-leader.rationale: The project extends democratic accountability and checks beyond the state, which is opposed to a leader bypassing deliberative institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: Cosmopolitan democracy wants more democratic institutions, including new ones above the state, so it denies the state is unnecessary or harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the project's nonviolence principle and liberal-left leanings; domestic gun law is not discussed.

empower-police-military.rationale: The project stresses restraint of force and arms control, so more domestic funding and authority for security forces is not a priority.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; liberal adherents divide on it.

decide-locally.rationale: Held wants decisions made at the level of those affected, which can mean local or global depending on the issue, so the statement as a general rule is split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from a human-rights orientation and liberal-left leanings; penal policy is not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: Liberal-cosmopolitan outlook is not tied to traditional family structures, though the sources are silent.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the equal-rights and universal-citizenship outlook; the sources do not mention it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the liberal-left outlook; the project itself takes no stand.

more-religion-public.rationale: Secular, universal-rights framing suggests adherents want no larger public religious role; not discussed directly.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from equal-rights and global-justice commitments; domestic remedies are not discussed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The project has no position on gender theory.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Archibugi argues the nation-state is losing its power and that belonging should extend beyond it, so national culture preservation is not a priority, though cultural pluralism is accepted.

gradual-change.rationale: Archibugi favours an incremental path of reforming existing institutions rather than utopian redesign, though he does demand deep change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Archibugi proposes a thin cosmopolitan citizenship with passports for refugees, which points against restriction, but migration levels are not discussed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The core programme is to democratise and strengthen the UN and related bodies; Archibugi urges that the UN be reclaimed and made to carry out its tasks.

free-trade.rationale: The sources stress democratic control of markets and global social democracy rather than endorsing or rejecting free trade.

nation-first.rationale: Cosmopolitan democracy holds that democracies apply double standards by refusing to share power internationally, and it seeks to subordinate national interest to global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Archibugi wants to enhance humanitarian intervention capacity, but only decided through cosmopolitan institutions that validate it, not unilateral force.

open-borders.rationale: The proposed thin global citizenship does not amount to open borders, and adherents are divided over it.

limit-growth.rationale: Environment appears only through global assemblies on climate; no case for limiting growth is made in the sources.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate is a standard example of a global problem needing democratic global governance, and a 2021 global citizens' assembly was held at COP26.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nonviolence is one of Archibugi's three principles and he favours peaceful, incremental reform.

experts-over-public.rationale: Held warned against technocrats ruling over everybody, so adherents prefer democratic voice over expert rule.

central-planning.rationale: Held's model is a social-democratic one working with markets under democratic law; central planning is not discussed.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not discussed; ownership form is not part of the project.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from global social-democratic leanings, with no source stating it.

basic-income.rationale: Archibugi proposes basic income entitlements for vulnerable groups such as refugees, so adherents are sympathetic though not to a universal national scheme specifically.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The project favours cooperative global rules over national protection, but trade policy is not discussed.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Held's social-democratic position is far from abolishing money and wage labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A global social democrat would back, not abolish, democratically accountable economic institutions.

one-party-rule.rationale: Democracy is the project's core value; Archibugi grounds it in popular control and equal participation rights.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Popular-control principle makes hereditary rule hard to defend, but monarchy is not discussed.

democracy-best.rationale: Archibugi describes democracy as the only available political system and a universal value, and the project extends it globally.

direct-votes.rationale: Held holds that democratic practice should fit each issue, mixing direct participation and representatives, so there is no blanket preference.

workers-councils.rationale: Not discussed; the project works through reformed representative and international institutions.

right-to-secede.rationale: Archibugi says cosmopolitan institutions could adjudicate self-determination claims, so there is neither a blanket right nor a ban.

natural-rulers.rationale: Equal political participation is one of Archibugi's principles, which rules out natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nonviolence is a founding principle for Archibugi, though adherents accept force authorised by legitimate institutions.

war-builds-character.rationale: The project aims at peace and arms control, and sees force only as a last resort.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from the universal-rights, secular outlook; not discussed.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Legitimate law rests on popular control and universal democratic procedure, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The project builds public courts and a global rule of law, such as expanded ICC jurisdiction, and rejects private provision of defence.

military-superiority.rationale: Adherents favour arms control and collective institutions over national military dominance.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Cosmopolitan citizenship and political community beyond the nation conflict with ethnic nationhood.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Held's reformist social democracy does not treat class conflict as history's main driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Social-democratic justice concerns are present but no source states an equal-outcomes goal.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not discussed; Archibugi does say institutions should represent minorities and cultural communities.

civilizational-union.rationale: Political community is envisaged as universal and layered, not drawn along civilizational lines.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The project asks democracies to stop applying double standards of self-interest abroad.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Cosmopolitan democracy rests on universal individual rights and equal participation, so communal duties are not placed first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is not part of the project.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The outlook is reformist and pro-modernity, aiming to govern globalisation democratically rather than reject it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not discussed; Held's Gridlock concerns governance lagging behind interdependence, not technology speed.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Held opposed rule by technocrats and the project stresses popular control, so handing decisions to algorithms runs against it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Archibugi presents the project as forward-looking reform of political community, the opposite of restoring a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Archibugi is pragmatic and incremental, but the project is also a principled democratic programme.

direct-action.rationale: Change is sought through institutional reform, public scrutiny and reformed international bodies, though social movements are credited as agents.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nonviolence and democratic procedure are both aim and method for Archibugi, and he rejects exporting democracy by force.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Wholly outside the outlook of a modernising institutional-reform project.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: No source suggests it, and it is far from social-democratic reform.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Held's justice concerns are social-democratic, not an explicit need-based communist principle.

production-for-use.rationale: The project accepts markets under democratic law rather than replacing profit with use-production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Reformist social democracy does not hold that profit is inherently exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dictatorial rule by any class contradicts the democratic principles of popular control and equal participation.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed and out of line with the reformist outlook.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Archibugi blames the structure of an oligarchic interstate order and democracies' double standards, not capitalism as such.

taxation-theft.rationale: A global social democrat accepts taxation as legitimate democratic redistribution.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal-democratic outlook is compatible with it, but the sources do not discuss it.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Archibugi wants representation for cultural communities and minorities as well as individuals, so adherents are mixed on group rights.

conscription.rationale: The project stresses arms reduction and restraint of force; conscription is not discussed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Archibugi's whole argument is that popular voice must be recovered through democratic structures.

state-as-business.rationale: Opposes technocratic and market rule over democratic citizenship.

positive-liberty.rationale: Held's global social democracy treats justice and well-being, not only non-interference, as necessary for effective freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Archibugi's critique targets states, the US and unaccountable economic actors, not media or universities.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Cosmopolitanism rests on equal moral worth; no source addresses the claim.

organic-representation.rationale: The project builds individual-based democratic representation, including a world parliament, not corporate or family representation.

total-state.rationale: Democratic participation and limited global powers conflict with a state directing all of life.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Archibugi rejects spreading anything by force and seeks restraint of interstate aggression, which is to be made a criminal matter.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Incompatible with popular control and equal participation.

bound-labor.rationale: Incompatible with equal rights and universal citizenship.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Universalist outlook; Archibugi stipulates democratic values as universal rather than as power-relative.

universal-morality.rationale: Cosmopolitanism claims universal moral standing for every person, and Archibugi treats democracy as a universal value.

single-common-good.rationale: Held stresses overlapping communities with differing interests deciding through democratic procedure rather than one reasoned common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; self-determination claims are to be adjudicated by cosmopolitan institutions, so no blanket position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not discussed; Archibugi favours passports and rights for refugees but not a diaspora return rule.

revive-national-language.rationale: Archibugi discusses multilingualism in a world polity, not national language revival.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Extending democratic say to economic life fits the global social-democratic aim of subjecting economic power to democracy, though firms are not discussed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is outside the cosmopolitan-democracy texts, and adherents range from liberal to social-democratic views on vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Social-democratic leanings favour stimulus when needed; not discussed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Held's model ties democracy to social justice and democratic control of markets rather than to economic freedom as a precondition.

rule-by-example.rationale: The project depends on legal and institutional constraints on rulers, such as criminal liability.

national-self-determination.rationale: Archibugi says cosmopolitan institutions should adjudicate self-determination claims, so the right is neither absolute nor denied.

force-without-un.rationale: Archibugi calls the UN the pivot of the world system and wants force validated by cosmopolitan institutions, and he opposes democracy by force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The project is about institutions, not epistemology, so adherents are free to hold religious or secular views on this.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Archibugi proposes universal rights and basic income entitlements for refugees, which cut against citizen-only welfare.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not discussed; the social-democratic stance leans against conditionality.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: No support in the sources for destroying cultural institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: The project works through universal institutions, not blocs of dominated states, though it criticises great-power dominance.

workers-nation.rationale: Transcending the nation is central, so organising only along national lines is not favoured.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Equal participation and universal rights principles exclude gender-distinct legal roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Out of line with the social-democratic outlook.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Equal participation rights and universal citizenship forbid it.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Archibugi sees states as democratisable and accountable, not merely tools of a ruling class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Global environmental governance is part of the agenda, but energy policy is not discussed.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Archibugi's thin citizenship and respect for cultural communities point away from forced assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no basis in the sources and opposed to the outlook.

proportional-representation.rationale: Held applies democratic procedure to fit each setting; proportional systems suit the inclusive-representation aim but are not stated.

national-mission.rationale: Archibugi argues explicitly against democracy being exported by force and against democracies' double standards.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from equal-rights outlook; not discussed.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Archibugi criticises unaccountable power, but not as corruption of national elites specifically.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Violates universal rights and equal moral standing.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Archibugi would hold individual leaders criminally liable and expand compulsory jurisdiction of courts.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Held's global social democracy requires far more than a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts equal moral worth and universal rights.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Moral cosmopolitanism holds every person is of equal moral standing, and SEP presents this as its core.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Held's reformist social democracy does not use the revolutionary-socialist question of building socialism in one country.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conflicts with the rights framework and equal participation.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; a religiously based legal ban is out of line with liberal pluralism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from secular universalism; not discussed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Opposed to the Leninist account of the state and in favour of democratic accountability.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Archibugi's thesis is that popular sovereignty must be recovered through democratic structures, extending consent to those affected by global decisions.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilism is at odds with cooperative global economic rules, but unaddressed.

population-transfer.rationale: Violates universal rights and equal participation.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Nonviolence is a principle but force is allowed as a last resort and through legitimate institutions, so the absolute libertarian rule does not fit.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The project aims at peaceful cooperation between peoples, not struggle as the engine of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed; democracy-protection views vary among liberal democrats.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Archibugi's critique of oligarchy and unaccountable power resembles non-domination, but he does not use the idea.

separated-powers.rationale: Cosmopolitan institutions are to supplement and constrain state institutions, a layered system of checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Contradicts popular control and equal participation.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Held's global justice concerns point this way, though the sources do not state it in these terms.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is a national policy matter the sources never touch, and adherents split on it.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred from the social-democratic stance; not discussed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The project locates global problems in governance, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Archibugi accepts and seeks representation for cultural communities and minorities in a plural global polity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Citizens' assemblies appear, but the sources treat them as complements to elected institutions, not replacing election.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The project holds states to criminal liability and legal accountability, opposing suspension of protections.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Emergency price policy is not covered in the sources and has no clear line from the project's principles.

party-controls-media.rationale: Incompatible with public scrutiny and transparency, one of Archibugi's principles.

party-commands-army.rationale: Incompatible with democratic control of force.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Thin cosmopolitan citizenship leans against long barriers to membership, though not discussed directly.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Legislators' pay is not addressed by the project, and no principle it states decides the question.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party organisation is not part of the project, so adherents have no common line.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Archibugi places the project between confederation and world federation with states sharing authority, and the EU is a standard model; the sources describe pooling, not the EU specifically.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Favours accountable, constrained power, but presidential systems are not discussed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance falls outside a political programme about global democratic institutions.

clerical-rule.rationale: Contradicts popular control and equal participation.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not a position of the project, which seeks legal restraint of war through institutions.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Public scrutiny and liberal rights outlook oppose it, though not stated.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Popular control and peaceful succession are among Archibugi's principles, which leans against unlimited tenure.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is a domestic device the sources do not discuss, though Archibugi's popular-control principle is compatible with it.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The project favours collective multilateral institutions, not unilateral withdrawal from alliances, but has not discussed alliances.

people-in-arms.rationale: The project aims at arms control and restraint of force.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Self-determination questions go to cosmopolitan institutions to adjudicate, so no blanket position.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not part of the outlook; Held was an academic reformist.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Archibugi stresses representation of cultural communities in a plural polity, which fits cultural parity, but is not stated in these words.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the human-rights orientation and the ICC model; not discussed.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from liberal equal-rights outlook; not discussed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not discussed; secular universalist outlook suggests no.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Censorship questions are not addressed, and liberal adherents split on obscenity law.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: A thin cosmopolitan citizenship and layered membership lean away from descent-based citizenship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Archibugi discusses multilingualism and representation of minorities and cultural communities in a global polity.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemption law is not discussed, and the equal-rights tradition pulls in both directions on it.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Held's global social-democratic concerns suggest sympathy, but debt is not discussed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: This is a dependency-theory claim, which neither Held nor Archibugi make in the sources.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from the popular-sovereignty principle; the sources do not discuss constitution-making.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Archibugi is skeptical of rapid democracy promotion yet defends political freedoms as universal; a restriction for growth would deny equal participation.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: SEP's moral cosmopolitans hold duties of aid are global in scope, and Held advocated global social democracy for justice and well-being, though Archibugi pays it little attention.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The project favours arms control and collective security over national nuclear forces.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Domestic constitutional design for presidents is not covered, so the project gives no answer.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The sources do not discuss monetary institutions, and adherents would divide between independence and democratic control.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The project favours negotiated, institutionally adjudicated settlements over hard territorial claims, but is not specifically discussed.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Fits Held's social-democratic subordination of markets to justice; not stated in these words.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism that cosmopolitan democracy does not engage.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from support for global environmental governance; not discussed.

collective-defense.rationale: The project is built on collective institutions and security, though adherents stress UN authorisation over alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Archibugi would restrain interstate aggression and hold leaders criminally liable.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state law is not covered in the sources and liberal adherents split on how far to curb religious bodies.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Ceremonial versus political heads of state is a domestic design question the project does not address.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Archibugi wants self-determination claims adjudicated by cosmopolitan institutions rather than settled by force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Layered, differentiated authority fits the project, but this specific arrangement is not discussed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contradicts popular control and equal participation.

character-from-environment.rationale: A question of psychology, not politics; the project makes no claim about it.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The project's core is legal accountability of rulers, including criminal liability for leaders.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy has no connection to the project's institutional agenda.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not engaged by the sources, which focus on layered democratic institutions.

leader-cult.rationale: Contradicts popular control and scrutiny of leaders.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court presumptions are outside the project and liberal adherents divide on them.

land-redistribution.rationale: Agrarian reform is a national policy question absent from the sources.

refugee-return.rationale: Archibugi supports passports and rights for refugees, which fits a return right, though return is not discussed.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Contradicts the aim of restraining interstate aggression and the rejection of ethnic community.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Violates universal rights and equal participation.

common-currency.rationale: Pooling sovereignty in common institutions fits, but currency is not discussed.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Political community is envisaged as universal and not along ancestry lines.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Archibugi accepts representation of cultural communities and minorities, though within state structures is not discussed.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Fits universal rights and equal participation wherever one lives; not discussed.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The reformist outlook sees institutional design as the lever of change, not material conditions alone.

ban-cartels.rationale: Fits subjecting concentrated economic power to democratic control; not discussed.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not addressed, and social-democratic leanings pull against a blanket ban.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Cosmopolitan institutions are meant to constrain national decisions, including by majorities, so adherents resist unconstrained national majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Equal participation is a principle, but quotas are not discussed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs contradict the project's global interdependence premise.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Held's global social democracy aims to embed markets in democratic law, which fits binding standards in trade rules.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Follows from equal political participation, though not discussed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Opposes nation-centred community, but curricula are not discussed.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Archibugi rejects imposing democracy by force and criticises great-power dominance of the international order.

patriotic-education.rationale: Cosmopolitan identity is the aim, but schooling is not discussed.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is a national policy debate the sources do not mention, and adherents split.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is not discussed in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Reformist social democracy assumes capitalism can be reformed rather than collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Archibugi criticises oligarchic great-power dominance and double standards.

delink-world-market.rationale: The project seeks democratic governance of global interdependence rather than withdrawal from it.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Conflicts with equal rights and universal citizenship.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The project aims at binding rights and courts, including expanded ICC and ICJ jurisdiction, that constrain governments.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The sources do not address the validity of colonial-era treaties, so there is no stated line.

elective-rulers.rationale: Popular control and peaceful succession through elections are core principles.

minority-veto.rationale: Held's model is democratic decision by those affected, not individual consent vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The project holds rulers criminally accountable through institutions, but nonviolence cuts against forcible resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Archibugi wants cosmopolitan institutions to constrain states, so national parliamentary supremacy is not endorsed.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not part of the project, though liberal cosmopolitans often accept it.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed and the project has no position.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The justice-based approach rests on rights and democratic redistribution, not elite paternalism.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The project is a call for broader political participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: This Frankfurt-school critique is not part of Held's or Archibugi's argument.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim about hegemony that the sources do not engage, though Archibugi criticises unaccountable power.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Archibugi does not discuss this and Held did not adopt dependency theory, though the project criticises unequal global power.

native-born-offices.rationale: Conflicts with equal participation and thin cosmopolitan citizenship.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns communist parties and is not part of the project.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Global social-democratic concerns favour international support, not self-reliance only.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The project restrains aggression and refers territorial claims to institutions.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Equal political participation points against group-based leadership claims.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Commitment to democracy and equal rights is compatible, though constitutional design is not discussed.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The sources do not take part in the debate over comparing fascism and communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historical claim outside the project; adherents follow mainstream scholarship.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Commemoration policy is a national matter the sources do not address.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not discussed in the sources, and the project makes no claim about gendered disadvantage.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: A domestic social-policy dispute outside the project's scope.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Archibugi treats democracy as a universal value, though he accepts authoritarian states can join global institutions and is skeptical of fast democratisation.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The project demands democratic control of force.

paid-care-work.rationale: Care work is not discussed in the sources, though the global social-democratic strand might sympathise.

filial-duty.rationale: Family duties are not addressed by a project about global democratic institutions.

office-by-exam.rationale: Popular control is central, though this is not discussed.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Fits economic nationalism, which is not the project's approach.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from liberal outlook; not discussed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The imperative-mandate model of delegation is not part of the proposals, which use reformed representative and advisory bodies.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Social-democratic leanings favour public systems, but not discussed.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Accountability of power to representative bodies is core, though budgets are not specifically discussed.

single-official-language.rationale: Archibugi addresses multilingualism in a world polity and favours accommodating linguistic pluralism.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Cosmopolitan outlook is against such restrictions, though not discussed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Legal tests of discrimination are not discussed in the sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: A cultural-critique claim that the sources do not make.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Archibugi opposes exporting democracy by force and wants force validated by international institutions.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Contradicts the restraint of interstate aggression and criminal liability for leaders.

corporate-influence.rationale: Held feared a few wealthy technocrats ruling over everybody, so adherents see excess corporate power as a democratic problem.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The project values transnational civil society and transparency, though funding rules are not discussed.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Not part of the outlook and counter to thin cosmopolitan citizenship.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not discussed; cosmopolitan outlook leans against residency-based exclusion.

democratic-peace.rationale: Archibugi argues democracies apply double standards abroad and endorses democracy as the universal system, but rejects spreading it by force.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The project depends on law and legitimate institutions that should be obeyed.

non-intervention.rationale: Archibugi wants cosmopolitan institutions to be able to decide on humanitarian intervention and hold leaders liable, contradicting absolute non-intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not a topic in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Contrary to equal rights and pluralism.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage law is not discussed, and the project has no stance.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Public scrutiny and transparency is one of Archibugi's three principles of popular control.

local-production.rationale: The project embraces interdependence over localisation.

informal-organisation.rationale: Reform proceeds through formal institutions, though civil society is a recognised agent.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Cosmopolitan institutions are meant to supplement and constrain state institutions on global issues.

religious-nation.rationale: Contradicts equal participation and universal citizenship.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Archibugi criticises oligarchic great-power dominance and double standards in international order.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Global social-democratic concerns favour sharing resources, though not discussed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A communist-theory formulation the project does not engage.

defeat-communism.rationale: Archibugi is skeptical of rapid democratisation and would let authoritarian states join global institutions, but no source frames this.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service delivery models are not covered, though social-democratic adherents would accept pluralism.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not addressed; a pluralist outlook would not take that line.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The sources do not make a historical judgement on capitalism, and adherents split between social-democratic and liberal readings.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not addressed, and adherents vary from liberal-reformist to social-democratic views.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of care work is not discussed in the sources.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Opposed to linguistic nationalism, though not stated.

treaties-binding.rationale: Respect for international law and agreements fits the project, though internal treaties are not discussed.

majority-settlement.rationale: Conflicts with equal rights and representation of minorities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Held's social democracy is a reformed market order, which is not exactly a third way as the statement means it.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Territorial claims should be adjudicated by institutions rather than rest on history.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Contradicts mainstream scholarship and the universal-rights outlook.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Contradicts popular control and equal participation.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Conflicts with universal rights and pluralism.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Archibugi criticises the oligarchy of powerful states and double standards.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religious doctrine is outside the project.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Held says decisions should be made by those they affect, with direct participation or representatives fitted to the issue.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectional analysis is not part of Held's or Archibugi's argument.

assisted-dying.rationale: End-of-life law is a national issue absent from the sources, and liberal adherents divide.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not addressed; Held identified with social democracy.

alienated-labor.rationale: This is a Marxian concept the project does not use.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Archibugi treats democracy as a universal value and cosmopolitanism rejects civilizational essentialism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Popular sovereignty is the basis of authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Dress rules in state institutions are not discussed, and liberal adherents divide between neutrality and religious freedom.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace-law detail is outside the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Held's global social democracy combines markets with justice, social protection and democratic law.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Archibugi favours arms control and enhanced humanitarian capacity, not abolition.

rich-first.rationale: Global social-justice orientation opposes that approach.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; collective multilateral institutions are favoured over blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Contradicts popular control and peaceful succession through democratic means.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist monetary theory is not part of the project.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Held's global-justice concerns might favour reforming lender rules, but the sources do not take a line on austerity refusal.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim the sources do not address.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept the project does not engage.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Held feared economic power ruling everybody, but the press is not discussed.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The project rests on legal accountability and rule of law, including in international relations.

online-participation.rationale: The 2021 global citizens' assembly is an example of wider participation; online methods are not discussed.

open-government-data.rationale: Public scrutiny and transparency is a principle of popular control.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Contrary to equal rights and pluralism.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The article describes a 2021 global citizens' assembly as a body that can claim to represent the global population.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious doctrine is outside the project and adherents hold differing personal views.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Held's concern that a few wealthy technocrats could rule over everybody expresses it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The project builds courts and enforcement mechanisms, not abolition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Layered, shared authority fits, though not discussed.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not addressed by the project, though peaceful succession is one of Archibugi's principles.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed in the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Held's Gridlock concerns global threats, but no source names extinction risk as a top priority.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Internal religious governance is outside the project.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Those affected by decisions should participate, which suggests this, though Archibugi does not state it.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy is not discussed in the sources.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not discussed, though trade rules are a global-governance topic.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Arms control is favoured but this specific rule is not discussed.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The sources do not discuss basing of foreign forces.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Fits accountability of leaders for atrocity through courts, but is not discussed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, though social-democratic leanings are sympathetic.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Nonviolence is a principle but not pacifism; force is a last resort.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: A question in gender theory the project does not take up.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A feminist-theory dispute outside the project.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Cosmopolitan democracy is secular and procedural.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: A Zionist-theory question not addressed in the sources.

culture-before-state.rationale: A nationalist-theory question the project does not address.

god-not-male.rationale: A theological question outside the project.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: A feminist-theology question outside the project.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Boundary-drawing for ethnic units is not discussed, though Archibugi would send self-determination claims to cosmopolitan institutions.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from civil-society and social-democratic orientation.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The question concerns the definition of socialism, which the project does not argue about.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Utility ownership is not discussed in the sources.

second-chamber.rationale: Bicameral design at national level is not covered by the sources.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The article contrasts cosmopolitan democracy with world federalism and calls it confederal, but the statement concerns town confederations.

family-wage.rationale: Wage-setting rules are not addressed in the sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Financial privacy is outside the project, and liberal adherents divide.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online privacy is not addressed in the sources, and adherents divide between privacy and accountability.

person-over-state.rationale: Moral cosmopolitanism puts the individual as the basic unit of concern, though the statement is not directly addressed.

spiritual-nature.rationale: A metaphysical claim the project does not make.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Layered authority with guaranteed levels fits the project better than revocable powers.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning has no place in the sources.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; cosmopolitan identity stresses universal membership.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Archibugi would criminalise aggression and allow force as a last resort, but also supports validated humanitarian intervention.

communal-electorates.rationale: Equal participation by individuals is the standard, though minorities' representation is valued.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: A conspiracy view not found in the sources.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from support for global environmental governance.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from support for global environmental governance.

women-distinct-values.rationale: A claim of difference feminism the sources do not make.

arms-reduction.rationale: Supporters favour popular diplomacy and arms control over military force.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Public scrutiny and transparency are principles; secrecy conflicts with them.

capital-controls.rationale: The sources do not discuss capital movement, though Held favoured democratic regulation of markets.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The sources do not address domestic arms monopolies, though they favour accountable force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Not addressed, though Archibugi would make leaders rather than soldiers liable for aggression.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: A specific welfare tool the sources do not discuss.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are not covered in the sources.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Held's global social democracy would reform international economic rules for justice, but Archibugi says little on WTO and IMF.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Reform through existing institutions, not their destruction.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The sources describe no stance on pluralism of economic systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The sources do not address environmental economics.

internal-colonialism.rationale: A claim from dependency and regional theory the project does not engage.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Moral cosmopolitanism rests on a common human standing, though not stated as human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Public scrutiny and transparency favour it, though not stated.

religions-one-truth.rationale: A perennialist claim outside the project.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Arms control stance leans against retaining weapons, though unilateral disarmament is not discussed.

workers-own-party.rationale: Party formation is not part of the project, which relies on broad civil-society agents.

ban-fgm.rationale: Fits universal human rights, though not discussed.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal participation and universal rights principles favour equal legal capacity for women, though inheritance law is not discussed.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic classification question outside the project.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: A libertarian legal-theory proposal not discussed in the sources.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Not addressed; popular control points against unelected roles.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; liberal-rights outlook resists subordinating liberty.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from rights orientation.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Language requirements for immigrants are not discussed, though Archibugi does treat multilingualism seriously.

voter-id.rationale: Election administration at national level is not discussed.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Archibugi stipulates a minimal procedural democracy based on nonviolence, popular control and equal participation.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Conflicts with public scrutiny and transparency.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare-design choice not discussed, though Archibugi mentions basic income for vulnerable groups.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal political participation rights are a core principle.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: A contested sociological claim the project does not make.

race-social-construct.rationale: Mainstream scholarly view, though not discussed.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Archibugi would strengthen the criminal liability of individual leaders for aggression and expand compulsory jurisdiction of international courts.

missingStatements.text: Political leaders who commit aggression or atrocities should be tried before international criminal courts.
missingStatements.rationale: Archibugi would strengthen the criminal liability of individual leaders for aggression and expand compulsory jurisdiction of international courts.

missingStatements.text: Decisions that affect people in many countries should be made with a democratic voice for those affected, not only by their national governments.
missingStatements.rationale: The project's central claim is that decisions should include all those they affect, which national democracy alone cannot do.
missingStatements.declined: Abstract principle that is hard for other ideologies to answer distinctly; overlaps empower-international-orgs.

missingStatements.text: A directly elected world parliament should be created alongside the United Nations.
missingStatements.rationale: Archibugi proposes a World Parliamentary Assembly, initially advisory, as the place where world citizens are heard.

notes: Held and Archibugi differ in emphasis: Held pairs democracy with global social democracy and distributive justice, while Archibugi concentrates on political institutions and says little on economics (Torresi notes the gap with global-justice theory). Most economic answers are therefore low confidence.
